lead.tldr: SEC proposal may exempt infrastructure platforms from broker registration, lowering compliance costs for bridge and node operators • Revised PARITY Act removes stablecoin de‑minimis threshold, imposes $1 deemed basis and wash‑sale rules, impacting staking yields • Hyperbridge exploit shows cross‑chain bridges remain vulnerable, limited sell‑off limits loss but reputational risk persists • Bitcoin hovering near $70k as Trump’s Strait‑of‑Hormuz threat fuels hedging, upcoming US inflation data will steer short‑term direction • Coinbase’s UK DeFi portal demonstrates regulated DEX access, pressuring rivals to embed compliant on‑ramp solutions

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, today regulators eased broker registration rules, a bridge hack exposed cross‑chain risks, and Bitcoin’s price wrestled with geopolitical tension and oil‑driven optimism. Coinbase’s new UK DeFi portal shows how regulated platforms can safely tap the ecosystem while lawmakers revisit crypto tax policy.

top_signals.title: SEC Proposes Certain Crypto Interfaces Don’t Need to Register as Brokers
top_signals.summary: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission has issued a proposal that certain cryptocurrency interfaces would be exempt from broker registration requirements. The proposal distinguishes platforms that only provide technical infrastructure from those that act as brokers. By clarifying the regulatory scope, the SEC aims to reduce compliance burdens for infrastructure providers. This guidance could affect how institutional investors evaluate the regulatory risk of using such platforms.

top_signals.title: U.S. lawmakers take another swing at crypto tax policy with revised bill
top_signals.summary: U.S. lawmakers have re‑introduced the PARITY Act as a revised effort to overhaul the tax treatment of cryptocurrency transactions. The new draft eliminates the $200 de‑minimis threshold for stablecoin trades, establishes a $1 deemed basis for crypto assets, and expands wash‑sale rules to cover digital holdings. By separating passive staking income from active trading, the legislation seeks to provide clearer guidance for institutional investors on reporting and compliance requirements.

top_signals.title: A hacker created $1.2bn of counterfeit crypto. They only sold it for $237,000
top_signals.summary: A code exploit on the Hyperbridge cross‑chain bridge enabled a hacker to mint one billion counterfeit Polkadot DOT tokens on the Ethereum network. The forged tokens were valued at roughly $1.2 billion. The attacker was only able to liquidate about $237 k before the operation was detected. The breach underscores the persistent security vulnerabilities of cross‑chain bridges and the need for robust safeguards to protect institutional exposure.

top_signals.title: Trump’s threat sends Bitcoin near $70,000 but these four events will be crucial for the price this week
top_signals.summary: Bitcoin fell nearly 4% to just above $70,000 after President Trump threatened to block the Strait of Hormuz. The geopolitical risk prompted traders to buy protective put options, signaling heightened hedging activity. This week’s price trajectory will be influenced by U.S. inflation data and industrial production figures. Additional volatility may arise from central‑bank meetings that could affect monetary‑policy expectations.

top_signals.title: Korean crypto ‘revenge agencies’ say they’ll murder people for Tether despite ‘ringleader’ arrest
top_signals.summary: South Korean police have reported that organized “revenge agencies” are still providing on‑demand intimidation, assault and murder services in exchange for payments in the USDT stablecoin. The criminal groups continue to advertise these illicit services on Telegram and X despite the arrest of a suspected ringleader. They require deposits that range from $300 to $5,700 and claim to record the attacks for their clients. The persistence of such illicit activity highlights regulatory and reputational risks for institutions with exposure to USDT and underscores the need for enhanced AML monitoring.

top_signals.title: Coinbase adds ‘DeFi mullet’ to UK offering in drive to become an everything exchange
top_signals.summary: Coinbase has launched a decentralized exchange portal for UK customers, giving them access to DeFi protocols such as Uniswap and Aerodrome through the Coinbase app. The feature, dubbed a “DeFi mullet,” is part of Coinbase’s broader push to become an “everything exchange.” By embedding DeFi services within a regulated framework, Coinbase aims to demonstrate that decentralized finance can be offered safely to mainstream investors.

top_signals.title: Falling oil prices a ‘powerful catalyst’ for crypto price growth, say experts — but there’s a catch
top_signals.summary: Analysts note that the recent 14% decline in oil prices could serve as a powerful catalyst for a Bitcoin rally. They argue that lower energy costs for miners and reduced inflation expectations may push Bitcoin above $70,000. The projected price trajectory depends on sustained low oil prices and continued geopolitical stability in the Middle East, factors that institutional investors monitor closely.

top_signals.title: Trump-backed World Liberty Financial’s token plummets to all-time low as firm calls self-dealing accusations ‘FUD’
top_signals.summary: World Liberty Financial, a firm backed by former President Trump, saw its WLFI token fall to an all‑time low after it was used as collateral on the Dolomite lending protocol. The collateralization enabled the company to borrow $75 million of stablecoins, including its own USD1 token, creating a circular borrowing structure that left USD1 lenders unable to redeem their holdings. The arrangement has drawn criticism and the company has labeled the self‑dealing accusations as “FUD,” while a vote is scheduled to decide a phased unlock schedule for the token.

linkedin_post: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, The regulatory landscape in the United States is shifting in ways that matter for every crypto venture. The SEC has just issued a proposal that could free technical infrastructure platforms from broker registration. By drawing a line between pure infrastructure and services that act as brokers, the agency hopes to lower compliance costs for the builders of the ecosystem. For institutional investors this clarity could make it easier to assess risk when they partner with layer‑1 and layer‑2 providers. At the same time, Congress is moving on tax policy. The revised PARITY Act removes the $200 de‑minimis threshold for stablecoin trades, sets a $1 deemed basis for all crypto assets and expands wash‑sale rules to digital holdings. It also separates passive staking income from active trading. The result is a more predictable reporting framework that could accelerate institutional capital flowing into the space. Security remains a top priority. A recent exploit on the Hyperbridge cross‑chain bridge allowed a hacker to mint one billion counterfeit Polkadot DOT tokens on Ethereum, a theoretical value of $1.2 billion. The attacker managed to sell only $237 k before the breach was stopped, but the incident is a stark reminder that bridges are still a weak point. Robust audit processes and real‑time monitoring are essential to protect investor capital.
